title: Reading and Improving Code with AI
concepts: keeping an old name as a second name

ai_pair_moment.flaw: Asked to refactor Sam's stock checker chk(s, o) with clear names and exactly the same behaviour, the AI renamed it low_stock and changed the comparison from < 3 to <= LOW_LIMIT, and said the behaviour was the same. Asha's characterization test for an item with exactly 3 left failed (1 failed, 4 passed), so she put < back and kept the clear names. Renaming also broke her daily report (ImportError: cannot import name 'chk'), fixed by keeping chk as a second name. A later AI suggestion added sorted(), a feature nobody asked for, and her test for the order of the items failed. Asha then kept the comprehension, dropped sorted() and ran every test again (stock_v3.py, 5 passed).

changes: The chapter continues Asha's Corner Cafe story: she inherits Sam's old till and stock code, which has short names, magic numbers and no tests.

Each refactoring step is its own small module (till_v2.py, till_v3.py, till_final.py; stock_old.py to stock_final.py) with its own pytest file, so every step's test run is verified and the video can show each version and its run separately. The modules only define functions, so their verified output is empty.
Diffs are made with difflib.unified_diff from the standard library on two verified files, skipping each file's '# file:' comment line, so the diff output is the same on every run.
The failing pytest runs use --tb=no to keep the report short; pytest's own short summary still names the failing test.

Critic review (8.2/10) applied: the fixed comparison shown before its run, regression defined, a real Improve-stage result (stock_v3.py, the comprehension without sorted(), 5 passed), all five tests shown with correct line highlights, the as alias and a function's second name explained, the diff labels and n explained, every renamed name named in the diff, with_tax moving into the return explained, constants described as a PEP 8 convention, and the practice tiers each highlighted. The kitchen analogy stays in the lesson but is left out of the video to keep its length.
outstanding_issues: On a learner's computer, the error reports show the full path to the file instead of the short file name.
The narration uses a synthetic voice (Kokoro bm_lewis). The owner should watch the video once and flag any word the voice mispronounces; fixes go in the PRONOUNCE list in tools/voice.py.
